title: CYBRIK organizational-hierarchy common definitions v1
description: Shared vendor-neutral primitives for the W2-G organizational-hierarchy + external-authority-boundary packet (ADR-0007 model; contract delta D-1..D-8). Realizes the portable tenant<->org_node governance model of docs/architecture/org-hierarchy/02-domain-model.md: tiers are DATA (ordinal into a configured ladder; NO fixed tier names), each org_node belongs to exactly one tenant (OD-1), hierarchy is authority routing not raw-data access (INV-1), and an external authority (A05) is an exchange peer, never a super-admin (INV-2). REUSES the accepted v0.1 cybrik.common-defs.v1 / cybrik.data-marking.v1 by $ref WITHOUT modifying them. $id uses the RFC 2606 .example documentation domain; it is an identifier, not an endpoint. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION (v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA). Accepted at Gate W2-G (Codex under Founder delegation, 2026-07-24).

orgNodeId.description: Opaque, stable org_node identifier. Stable across reorg churn (02 §8): display labels change, this id does not. Never a tier name.

tierOrdinal.description: Ordinal depth into the deployment-configured tier ladder (02 §2.1). Tiers are DATA: the product ships NO fixed tier names (no 'district'/'province'/'commune'). A hard-coded administrative NAME is not expressible here — it is an integer ordinal, not a string. 3-4+ tiers are configuration.

labelKey.description: A label KEY the UI resolves from the deployment's locale catalog (VI/EN at minimum; 03 §2.1). The model stores keys; it never stores a hard-coded administrative display string.

labels.description: Display-label reference for a node/tier/role. Stores a catalog KEY (resolved per locale by the UI shell). An optional inline locale_labels map is provenance/fallback only; the catalog is authoritative.

locale_labels.description: Optional per-locale fallback strings, keyed by BCP-47 locale (e.g. 'vi', 'en'). Advisory: the label catalog resolves the authoritative display string.

boundaryKind.description: Whether a node is an internal governed tier or an external exchange peer. 'external' nodes (e.g. A05) are NOT administrable, are NOT in the internal tier ladder, and never appear as ancestors of internal nodes (INV-2; 02 §1.2, §4).

orgNodeStatus.description: Node lifecycle state (02 §1.2). There is deliberately NO 'deleted' state: a node referenced by audit history is never hard-deleted; 'archived' is the only terminal state (D-1; no-hard-delete-referenced-nodes). Rollback is a status transition, not a row delete.

residencyZone.description: Opaque data-residency / jurisdiction zone token (e.g. an ISO 3166 region code or a deployment-defined zone). Vendor/jurisdiction-neutral; no country is hard-coded in the schema (01 §5; 02 §8).

jurisdiction.description: Residency / jurisdiction expressed as policy-as-data, evaluated DENY-BY-DEFAULT (ADR-0007 OD-4). A crossing is permitted only into an explicitly allowed zone; an empty allowed_zones denies every crossing. Legal compulsion is a separate governed workflow with audit, never a standing grant here.

allowed_zones.description: The zones this data MAY be processed/exchanged into. Deny-by-default: a zone not listed is denied. An empty list denies all crossings (fail-closed).

orgNodeRef.description: A self-describing reference to a node, carrying its authoritative tenant and boundary so a relying party can enforce cross-tenant / external-boundary invariants without a second lookup. tenant_binding and boundary_kind are REQUIRED at any site where a cross-tenant or external-ancestor check is evaluated.

roleArchetype.description: The small set of capability archetypes a deployment-configurable role maps to (02 §1.3). A membership binds an actor to an org_node with one of these; it confers node-scoped capability, NOT descendant raw data access.

scopeKind.description: The hierarchical reach of a grant (02 §2.2). 'own-node' = the actor's node (raw, within tenant + need-to-know). 'descendant' = subtree, raw ONLY with an explicit descendant-read grant + need-to-know (INV-1). 'aggregate' = de-identified counts/metrics over the subtree, NO raw records (the default cross-tier visibility). 'delegated' = a single time-boxed object/case shared by another node.

subjectRelationship.description: How the grant subject relates to the target subtree — the INV-1 hinge. 'own-node'/'explicit-descendant-grant'/'delegated-object' may carry raw. 'ancestor-governance' (an ancestor's default cross-tier reach) carries GOVERNANCE ONLY: aggregate, never automatic raw (INV-1; 02 §0). A grant asserting ancestor-governance with a raw_scope is structurally rejected.

edgeType.description: Typed governance/exchange edge (02 §6). 'parent' = tier edge (up->down governance; tasking + aggregate roll-up + policy; NO raw read, INV-1). 'escalation' = down->up transfer/share of a specific object. 'tasking' = up->down authority-to-direct, NO read. 'case-delegation' = peer, scoped time-boxed object share. 'exchange' = across the external trust boundary.

exchangeDirection.description: Explicit external-exchange direction (02 §4). Distinct authorization per direction. 'outbound-submission' = report up to the external authority. 'inbound-directive' = the external authority tasks us; it NEVER auto-executes and enters the normal policy/approval/tool path.

grantMechanism.description: How authority was conferred. 'standard' = an ordinary explicit grant. 'break-glass' = the pre-authorized, role-gated, loud, self-revoking emergency path (ADR-0007 OD-6): default read-only, 15-minute default TTL, 60-minute maximum requiring a second human approval, mandatory high-severity audit + oversight notification, mandatory after-action review. Never a hierarchy backdoor.

smallCellFloor.description: Configurable small-cell suppression floor for de-identified aggregates (ADR-0007 OD-2). Const 5: an unsuppressed aggregate cell counting fewer than 5 underlying subjects is a re-identification risk and is not expressible. No differential privacy is adopted here (separately evaluated).

grantTemporal.description: Temporal + revocation envelope shared by every grant (membership, scope grant, delegation, exchange authorization, break-glass). Every grant is expiring and revocable; idempotent replay after expiry/revocation MUST NOT re-authorize (02 §5.4; ADR-0006 E3 semantics).

max_uses.description: Optional cap on the number of authorizations this grant may back before it is spent.

revoked.description: Immediate, audited revocation flag. A revoked grant authorizes nothing even within its window.

separation_of_duties.description: When true, the grantor/approver MUST be distinct from the subject; self-authorization is rejected (runtime).

audit_ref.description: Opaque reference to the audit record for this grant's issuance. Required by the relying party for every grant that reaches raw data or crosses the external boundary.

needToKnow.description: The object-level predicate layered on top of scope (02 §2.5): scope says 'you could reach this subtree'; need-to-know says 'you may read THIS record, for THIS purpose, now'. Mirrors delegation-chain purpose/scope (ADR-0006 E3).

purpose.description: Bounded purpose binding for the read (e.g. an assigned case or investigation).

case_refs.description: The specific product-owned objects this need-to-know covers, by digest-bound objectRef. Dereferenced through the owner's authorized API only.
